questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨5,3,-4⟩+t⟨-5,2,7⟩,\,Π:r\cdot ⟨2,3,1⟩=30.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's write the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨5-5t,3+2t,-4+7t⟩.
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨5-5t,3+2t,-4+7t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨2,3,1⟩ & =30 \\ ⟨5-5t,3+2t,-4+7t⟩\cdot ⟨2,3,1⟩ & =30 \\ 2(5-5t)+3(3+2t)-4+7t & =30 \\ 10-10t+9+6t-4+7t & =30 \\ 3t & =15 \\ t & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$ is obtained by substituting $t=5$ into the equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨5-5(5),3+2(5),-4+7(5)⟩ \\  & =⟨-20,13,31⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(-20,13,31).$

questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨3,0,-1⟩+t⟨5,-2,4⟩,\,Π:r\cdot ⟨0,1,-2⟩=22.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's write the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨3+5t,-2t,-1+4t⟩.
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨3+5t,-2t,-1+4t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨0,1,-2⟩ & =22 \\ ⟨3+5t,-2t,-1+4t⟩\cdot ⟨0,1,-2⟩ & =22 \\ 0(3+5t)+1(-2t)+(-2)(-1+4t) & =22 \\ -2t+2-8t & =22 \\ -10t & =20 \\ t & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$ is obtained by substituting $t=-2$ into the equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨3+5(-2),-2(-2),-1+4(-2)⟩ \\  & =⟨-7,4,-9⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(-7,4,-9).$

$$
r=⟨1+5t,1+2t,1-4t⟩.

Now, substituting $r=⟨1+5t,1+2t,1-4t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨2,-3,5⟩ & =36 \\ ⟨1+5t,1+2t,1-4t⟩\cdot ⟨2,-3,5⟩ & =36 \\ 2(1+5t)-3(1+2t)+5(1-4t) & =36 \\ 2+10t-3-6t+5-20t & =36 \\ -16t & =32 \\ t & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$ is obtained by substituting $t=-2$ into the equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨1+5(-2),1+2(-2),1-4(-2)⟩ \\  & =⟨-9,-3,9⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨3,2,7⟩+t⟨-5,-6,0⟩,\,Π:r\cdot ⟨-6,5,4⟩=-24.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's write the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨3-5t,2-6t,7⟩.
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨3-5t,2-6t,7⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨-6,5,4⟩ & =-24 \\ ⟨3-5t,2-6t,7⟩\cdot ⟨-6,5,4⟩ & =-24 \\ -6(3-5t)+5(2-6t)+4\cdot 7 & =-24 \\ -18+30t+10-30t+28 & =-24 \\ 20 & =-24.\end{aligned}
$$

The equation has no solution. Therefore, we conclude that the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ do not intersect.

questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨5,-2,3⟩+t⟨0,3,-1⟩,\,Π:r\cdot ⟨1,3,-2⟩=-7.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's write the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨5,-2+3t,3-t⟩.
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨5,-2+3t,3-t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨1,3,-2⟩ & =-7 \\ ⟨5,-2+3t,3-t⟩\cdot ⟨1,3,-2⟩ & =-7 \\ 5+3(-2+3t)+(-2)(3-t) & =-7 \\ 5-6+9t-6+2t & =-7 \\ 11t & =0 \\ t & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$ is obtained by substituting $t=0$ into the equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨5,-2+3(0),3-0⟩ \\  & =⟨5,-2,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(5,-2,3).$

questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:{\begin{aligned}x=5-t \\ y=4+2t \\ z=-6-3t\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,Π:4x+6y-3z-130=0.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We can substitute the parametric expressions for $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ of the line into the equation of the plane immediately:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x+6y-3z-130 & =0 \\ 4(5-t)+6(4+2t)-3(-6-3t) & =130 \\ 20-4t+24+12t+18+9t & =130 \\ 17t & =68 \\ t & =4\end{aligned}
$$

To get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$, we substitute $t=4$ into the parametric equations of the line:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5-4=1 \\ y=4+2(4)=12 \\ z=-6-3(4)=-18\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection point is  $P(1,12,-18).$

\begin{aligned}x-3y+2z & =12 \\ 1(7+2t)-3(3+t)+2(1-t) & =12 \\ 7+2t-9-3t+2-2t & =12 \\ -3t & =12 \\ t & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

To get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$, we substitute $t=-4$ into the parametric equations of the line:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=7+2(-4)=-1 \\ y=3+(-4)=-1 \\ z=1-(-4)=5\end{aligned}

questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨2,1,0⟩+t⟨1,3,2⟩,\,Π:3x-2y+4z+6=0.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨2+t,1+3t,2t⟩.
$$

Let's also write the equation of the plane in the dot product form:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x-2y+4z+6 & =0 \\ 3x-2y+4z & =-6 \\ ⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨3,-2,4⟩ & =-6 \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-2,4⟩ & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨2+t,1+3t,2t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨3,-2,4⟩ & =-6 \\ ⟨2+t,1+3t,2t⟩\cdot ⟨3,-2,4⟩ & =-6 \\ 3(2+t)-2(1+3t)+4(2t) & =-6 \\ 6+3t-2-6t+8t & =-6 \\ 5t & =-10 \\ t & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P,$ we substitute $t=-2$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨2+(-2),1+3(-2),2(-2)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-5,-4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(0,-5,-4).$

questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨-1,-2,6⟩+t⟨2,5,4⟩,\,Π:x+2y+z-33=0.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨-1+2t,-2+5t,6+4t⟩.
$$

Let's also write the equation of the plane in the dot product form:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2y+z-33 & =0 \\ x+2y+z & =33 \\ ⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨1,2,1⟩ & =33 \\ r\cdot ⟨1,2,1⟩ & =33\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨-1+2t,-2+5t,6+4t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨1,2,1⟩ & =33 \\ ⟨-1+2t,-2+5t,6+4t⟩\cdot ⟨1,2,1⟩ & =33 \\ -1+2t+2(-2+5t)+6+4t & =33 \\ -1+2t-4+10t+6+4t & =33 \\ 16t & =32 \\ t & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨-1+2(2),-2+5(2),6+4(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨3,8,14⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(3,8,14).$

questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨3,0,-4⟩+t⟨2,4,3⟩,\,Π:4x+3y+4z-60=0.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨3+2t,4t,-4+3t⟩.
$$

Let's also write the equation of the plane in the dot product form:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x+3y+4z-60 & =0 \\ 4x+3y+4z & =60 \\ ⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨4,3,4⟩ & =60 \\ r\cdot ⟨4,3,4⟩ & =60\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨3+2t,4t,-4+3t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨4,3,4⟩ & =60 \\ ⟨3+2t,4t,-4+3t⟩\cdot ⟨4,3,4⟩ & =60 \\ 4(3+2t)+3(4t)+4(-4+3t) & =60 \\ 12+8t+12t-16+12t & =60 \\ 32t & =64 \\ t & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨3+2(2),4(2),-4+3(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨7,8,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(7,8,2).$

questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨-5,0,1⟩+t⟨-3,1,0⟩,\,Π:-3x+y-2z+27=0.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨-5-3t,t,1⟩.
$$

Let's also write the equation of the plane in the dot product form:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3x+y-2z+27 & =0 \\ -3x+y-2z & =-27 \\ ⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-3,1,-2⟩ & =-27 \\ r\cdot ⟨-3,1,-2⟩ & =-27\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨-5-3t,t,1⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨-3,1,-2⟩ & =-27 \\ ⟨-5-3t,t,1⟩\cdot ⟨-3,1,-2⟩ & =-27 \\ -3(-5-3t)+1\cdot t-2\cdot 1 & =-27 \\ 15+9t+t-2 & =-27 \\ 10t & =-40 \\ t & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P,$ we substitute $t=-4$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨-5-3(-4),-4,1⟩ \\  & =⟨7,-4,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(7,-4,1).$

questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨1,3,2⟩+w⟨-5,-2,-1⟩,\,Π:r=⟨-12,10,6⟩+s⟨1,0,4⟩+t⟨2,6,0⟩.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
From the equation of a plane in the parametric form $r=p+tv+sw$, we have that its normal vector is $n=v\times w.$ In our case, the normal vectors to $Π$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =v\times w \\  & =⟨1,0,4⟩\times ⟨2,6,0⟩ \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 2 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 6 & 0\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}|k \\  & =-24i+8j+6k \\  & =⟨-24,8,6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the plane $Π$ in dot product form is

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-24,8,6⟩ & =⟨-12,10,6⟩\cdot ⟨-24,8,6⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-24,8,6⟩ & =404.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨1,3,2⟩+w⟨-5,-2,-1⟩$ into the equation of the plane in dot product form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨-24,8,6⟩ & =404 \\ ⟨1-5w,3-2w,2-w⟩\cdot ⟨-24,8,6⟩ & =404 \\ -24(1-5w)+8(3-2w)+6(2-w) & =404 \\ -24+120w+24-16w+12-6w & =404 \\ 98w & =392 \\ w & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $q$ of the intersection point $Q,$ we substitute $w=4$ into the vector equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}q & =⟨1-5(4),3-2(4),2-(4)⟩ \\  & =⟨-19,-5,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection point is $Q(-19,-5,-2).$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨-7,5,1⟩ & =-65 \\ ⟨5+4t,3-2t,-4-3t⟩\cdot ⟨-7,5,1⟩ & =-65 \\ -7(5+4t)+5(3-2t)+(-4-3t) & =-65 \\ -35-28t+15-10t-4-3t & =-65 \\ -41t & =-41 \\ t & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the position vector $\mathbf{p}$ of the intersection point is obtained by substituting $t=1$ into the equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨5+4(1),3-2(1),-4-3(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨9,1,-7⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(9 , 1, -7).$

Now, substituting $\mathbf{r} = \langle 1+2t , 3+t, 1 \rangle$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨4,-3,2⟩ & =7 \\ ⟨1+2t,3+t,1⟩\cdot ⟨4,-3,2⟩ & =7 \\ 4(1+2t)-3(3+t)+2\cdot 1 & =7 \\ 4+8t-9-3t+2 & =7 \\ 5t & =10 \\ t & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $\mathbf{p}$ of the intersection point $P,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨1+2(2),3+(2),1⟩ \\  & =⟨5,5,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(5 , 5, 1).$
